scope: Reviewed all 36 files under agent/: Fastify service and routes, agent loop, classifier, tool registry/executor/approvals, MCP metadata scanner, EHR/payments/SMS/A2A integrations, kill switch, budgets, audit recorder, reminders worker, prompts, config, release manifest, Dockerfile, k8s manifests, Terraform (EKS, IAM, GitHub), CI/deploy workflows, CODEOWNERS and tests. Not found in the repo: .brace/ record, package-lock.json, .terraform.lock.hcl, egress-proxy rules, admission policy, staff approval console, monitoring/alerting, drift detection, and the EHR MCP and eligibility peer code. Those items are rated needs_evidence rather than gap. Code was read only; nothing was run. No injection attempts found in repo text. Reviewer model: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5). Normal mode, no --conservative. Step 8 challenges have NOT been run: all likely_pass and G1/G2 na_candidate ratings are unchallenged.

findings.title: Distinct agent identity
findings.requirement: Give the agent its own non-human identity. Keep it separate from the user who launched it and from unrelated agents. Show that permissions and revocation belong to that identity, even when a user starts the run.

not_covered.problem: Action records missing any of the six identity fields
Instance or tenant labels taken from what the model supplies
A credential scoped to more operations, resources, or tenants than needed
Revocation delay from cached or self-contained tokens not measured

evidence.note: Agent runs under its own service account and IAM role

checks.check: The agent runs under its own workload principal (service account, IAM role, SPIFFE ID, or agent ID) that no other service or unrelated agent uses.
checks.verify: 1) Find the agent's identity: pod `serviceAccountName`, IAM role, SPIFFE ID, or agent ID in IaC or deploy config. 2) Search other deployments, services, and agents in the repo for the same name or role. 3) Answer no if it is shared, `default`, the main backend's identity, or only a string label with no credential. Answer unknown if identity is assigned outside this repo.
checks.counter_search: Searched manifests and terraform for other users of the role; only the agent pods and its reminder job, which is the same agent, use it.
checks.note: Agent runs under its own service account and IAM role

checks.check: Tool and API clients get credentials from the agent's own principal, not from the launching user's forwarded token or session cookie.
checks.verify: 1) Find every place tool and API clients get a token or key. 2) Trace where each comes from: workload identity or token exchange, versus the incoming request's `Authorization` header or session cookie. 3) Check every client, not just the main one. 4) Answer no if any client forwards the user's token or cookie as-is, or uses a shared static key.
checks.counter_search: Traced EHR, payments, SMS and peer clients; all use workload token, token exchange or per-clinic service secrets, never the user JWT.
checks.note: Clients use agent credentials not forwarded user tokens

checks.check: When a user starts a run, the user is carried as a delegated subject (for example a token exchange with separate act and sub), while the agent keeps its own principal.
checks.verify: 1) Find the code that starts a run for a user. 2) Look for token exchange (RFC 8693, `subject_token`, `actor_token`, `act`/`sub` claims) or a separate delegated-subject field. 3) Check the agent's own principal is still the actor. 4) Answer no if the user's token is used directly or the user replaces the agent identity. Answer unknown if the exchange happens in an outside identity service.
checks.counter_search: Searched for user token use as agent identity; the user is a separate subject field and the actor stays the agent role.
checks.note: User carried as separate subject field

checks.check: Permissions are bound to the agent principal in IaC or RBAC, so revoking that principal alone removes the agent's access without disabling the user.
checks.verify: 1) Find IAM policies, RoleBindings, or grants in Terraform, Helm, or Kubernetes YAML. 2) Check they bind to the agent principal, not to a user, group, or shared role. 3) Check that removing that binding alone would cut the agent's access. 4) Answer no if access depends on the user's grants or a shared credential. Answer unknown if permissions are not defined in this repo.
checks.counter_search: Searched for user-bound grants; permissions attach to the runtime role and removing it cuts agent access without touching users.
checks.note: Permissions bind to the agent role in terraform

findings.summary: Agent has its own service account and IAM role separate from users.
findings.next_step: Drill disabling the role without affecting staff or patient sessions.

challenge.note: I found no failing control; the main weakness is that the eligibility token exchange encodes the patient only in the scope string rather than as a true delegated subject.

findings.title: All six identity fields

not_covered.problem: Identity labels taken from what the model supplies
Agent-type-id not computed as a hash of its identity inputs
Agent able to erase or rewrite its own audit history
Sub-agent record missing its parent link or parent prompt

findings.title: Content-derived type identity
findings.requirement: Compute the agent-type-id as a hash of the container digest, harness, system prompt, model ID and version, and configuration. The model part includes checkpoint and fine-tune or adapter references where they apply. Keep the list of inputs (the manifest) and the hashing steps. Check that changing any input changes the ID, and that the same manifest gives the same ID.

not_covered.problem: Changed running config still reporting the old approved ID
Hosted model changing behind a fixed name
Release manifest missing training job, dataset, or model provider records
Action records missing any of the six identity fields

evidence.note: Hash covers only .txt prompts, so prompts/system.md, the system prompt, is not in the agent-type-id

checks.check: The agent-type-id is a hash over a manifest that includes the container digest, harness, system prompt, model ID and version, and configuration.
checks.verify: 1) Find the code or CI step that computes `agent.type.id` (search `sha256`, `hashlib`, `createHash`, `type_id`). 2) List its inputs. 3) Check each is there: container digest, harness, system prompt, model ID and version, configuration. 4) Answer no if the ID is a label, version string, or git tag, or any input is missing.
checks.note: Hash covers only .txt prompts, so prompts/system.md, the system prompt, is not in the agent-type-id

checks.check: The hash covers every file that defines the prompt, tools, and configuration, with no file or directory skipped or excluded.
checks.verify: 1) Open the function that lists files to hash. 2) Write down every filter it applies: hidden files, names starting with '_' or '__', extensions, ignore lists, glob patterns. 3) For each filter, check whether a file that defines tools, prompts, or config would be skipped (for example `__init__.py`, `index.ts`, `.env`, `config/*.local.*`). 4) Answer no if any such file is skipped.
checks.note: Extension filter skips system.md; MCP server list in manifest.json is also not hashed

checks.check: The model input is a pinned version or snapshot (plus checkpoint and adapter references where used), not an alias and not the app's release number.
checks.verify: 1) Find the model ID that goes into the manifest or hash. 2) Follow env vars and config to the final value, including defaults such as `getenv('MODEL', ...)`. 3) Answer no if it is an alias (`-latest`, no date or version), falls back to one when unset, or is the app release number. Also no if adapters or checkpoints are used but left out.
checks.counter_search: Searched for env overrides and aliases; both model IDs are hard-coded dated snapshots with no fallback.
checks.note: Model IDs are pinned snapshots

checks.check: The manifest is put in a fixed, documented order before hashing, so the same manifest always gives the same ID.
checks.verify: 1) Open the serialization step before hashing. 2) Check for a fixed order: sorted keys (`sort_keys=True`), sorted file lists, fixed encoding and line endings. 3) Check file lists are not taken straight from directory listing or map iteration order. 4) Answer no if any unsorted dict, map, or filesystem order reaches the hash.
checks.counter_search: Checked for map or directory order reaching the hash; prompt list is sorted, config list is fixed, labels and NULs separate inputs.
checks.note: Fixed order manifest before hashing

checks.check: Secret values are not placed in the hashed manifest in a form that exposes them.
checks.verify: 1) List every value fed into the manifest or hash. 2) Check whether any are secrets: API keys, tokens, passwords, private keys, `.env` contents. 3) Answer no if a secret value is written in plain text to the stored manifest, or the whole environment is dumped into it.
checks.counter_search: Searched inputs for env dumps or secrets; only digest, version, sha, prompts, model ids and config yaml are hashed.
checks.note: No secret values in the hashed manifest

violates: Compute the agent-type-id as a hash of the container digest, harness, system prompt, model ID and version, and configuration

findings.next_step: Hash every prompt file including prompts/system.md and add a test that a prompt edit changes the id.

findings.title: Trustworthy attribution
findings.requirement: Assign instance and tenant identity in the trusted execution layer. Don't accept labels the model supplies. Record the delegated subject — the user or system whose authority is being used — separately from the agent's identity. Test that the agent can't pose as another instance or tenant in requests or audit records. Test that trace context survives handoffs between async jobs. Treat trace IDs and caller-supplied labels only as a way to link records. They never prove identity or permission.

not_covered.problem: Agent sharing the launching user's identity
Prompt a parent gave a sub-agent not recorded
Sub-agent authorized using an earlier actor's authority
Action records missing any of the six identity fields

evidence.note: Tool tenant uses the model-supplied clinicId even though audit tenant uses verified context

checks.check: Tenant and instance identity are set by the harness or platform from verified context, never from model-produced text or tool arguments.
checks.verify: 1) Find every place tenant and instance IDs are set for tool calls and records. 2) Check each comes from verified context (token claims, session bound at launch). 3) Check tool JSON schemas the model fills for `tenant_id`, `user_id`, `instance_id`. 4) Answer no if any function uses the model's value, even if another function uses verified context.
checks.quote: const clinicId = typeof input.clinicId === "string" && input.clinicId ? input.clinicId : ctx.tenantId;
checks.note: Tool tenant uses the model-supplied clinicId even though audit tenant uses verified context

checks.check: Tenant or instance labels in tool arguments or agent-controlled headers are rejected or overwritten with the verified values before they are used or logged.
checks.verify: 1) Find tool handlers and middleware that receive tool arguments and headers. 2) Check that tenant or instance fields in arguments, or headers like `X-Tenant-Id`, are rejected or overwritten with the verified value before use or logging. 3) Answer no if any handler uses or logs the supplied value, or detects a mismatch and continues.
checks.quote: const tenantId = (req.headers["x-clinic-id"] as string | undefined) ?? claims.clinic_id;
checks.note: x-clinic-id header is used instead of overwritten with the verified claim

checks.check: The delegated subject is recorded separately from the agent identity.
checks.verify: 1) Open the audit record schema and writer. 2) Look for a delegated-subject field (the user or system whose authority is used) separate from the agent principal field. 3) Answer no if only one identity is stored, the user overwrites the agent identity, or the field is never filled.

checks.counter_search: Looked for the user overwriting agent identity; subject is a separate field from agent type and instance ids.

checks.check: When work is handed to an async job or queue, the trusted layer attaches the verified attribution and trace context, and the job uses them.
checks.verify: 1) Find queue producers and enqueue calls (Celery, SQS, Pub/Sub, Kafka, cron). 2) Check the trusted layer adds verified identity and trace context to the job. 3) Check the worker uses those values, not ones the agent wrote. 4) Answer no if workers start new traces without parent context or take tenant from agent-written job data.

checks.counter_search: Searched for queues and async handoffs; only the cron job exists and it builds its own verified context from the clinic directory.

checks.check: Authorization never treats trace IDs or caller-supplied labels as proof of identity or permission.
checks.verify: 1) Find authorization and permission-lookup code. 2) Check what each decision is keyed on. 3) Answer no if any check uses a trace ID, span ID, correlation ID, request label, or caller-supplied header as identity or to look up permissions.
checks.quote: const tenantId = (req.headers["x-clinic-id"] as string | undefined) ?? claims.clinic_id;

Don't accept labels the model supplies

findings.title: Operational lookup
findings.requirement: Start from one suspicious action. Find the team responsible, the current operator, the deployment manifest, and the live instance. Show that you can contain the right instance or agent type without cutting off the launching user's other access.

not_covered.problem: Stop doesn't halt running work or open tool streams within a set time
No drill for a compromised shared tool or agent type
Action records missing any of the six identity fields

Answer unknown if the lookup store is outside this repo.

Answer unknown if ownership lives in an outside catalog.

Protect sensitive prompt text with restricted storage and a clear redaction policy. Standard GenAI instrumentation records prompts only when you turn that on, so confirm it is on for this path.

Children still running after the parent is stopped

findings.title: Minimal tool surface
findings.requirement: List every built-in tool, MCP server, API, program, and file permission this agent type can use. Give a task-based reason for each. Enforce a role-based allowlist, and check that an unlisted tool can't be called. Don't base allow or approval decisions on hints a server gives about its own tools, such as "read-only." MCP treats those hints as untrusted unless you trust the server.

not_covered.problem: A tool call that skips the MCP gateway or reaches a tool server directly
A token or credential with too much access
Hidden instructions inside a tool's description or schema
A tool's description or schema changing after it was approved
Lookalike or duplicate tool names across servers

evidence.note: One fixed allowlist of named tools for the single scheduling role

checks.check: Each agent role has one explicit allowlist of tool names, with no wildcard grants such as `*`, `mcp__*`, `Bash(*)`, or `bypassPermissions`.
checks.verify: 1) Find where each agent is built and tools are passed (`allowed_tools`, `tools=[`, `allowedTools`, `.mcp.json`, `settings.json`). 2) Check each role has one fixed list of names. 3) Answer no if any list holds `*`, `mcp__*`, `Bash(*)`, a pattern or regex, `bypassPermissions`, or is built from `list_tools()`, or if a second agent role or entry point has no list.
checks.counter_search: Searched allowlist yaml and executor for wildcards or list_tools-built lists; found one fixed named list.
checks.note: One fixed allowlist of named tools for the single scheduling role

checks.check: Tools discovered from MCP servers are filtered against that allowlist before the model can see or call them.
checks.verify: 1) Find MCP discovery (`list_tools`, `session.list_tools`, `tools/list`, MCP client setup). 2) Trace the result to where it is handed to the model. 3) Confirm a filter keeps only names on the allowlist. 4) Answer no if any discovered tool reaches the model unfiltered, the filter is a denylist or prefix match (`startswith`, `mcp__server__`), or a refresh or reconnect path skips it.
checks.note: All registered tools reach the model; no filter against the allowlist before the model sees them (executor still denies calls)

checks.check: The dispatcher rejects a call to any tool name not on the allowlist, instead of looking it up dynamically.
checks.verify: 1) Find the dispatcher (search `tool_use`, `call_tool`, `dispatch`, `execute`, `getattr`, `registry[`). 2) Check it rejects names not on the allowlist with an error. 3) Answer no if it looks tools up with `getattr`, `globals()`, `eval`, or a registry holding more than the allowlist, falls back to calling the MCP server directly, or catches the unknown-tool error and continues.
checks.counter_search: Searched for other dispatch paths, getattr-style lookups, direct MCP calls; executeTool is the only dispatcher.
checks.note: Dispatcher denies any name not on the allowlist before registry lookup

checks.check: Allow and approval decisions never read server-supplied hints or descriptions such as `readOnlyHint` or 'read-only'.
checks.verify: 1) Search for `readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `annotations`, `description`, and approval or auto-approve code. 2) Check whether any allow, skip-approval, or permission branch reads these. 3) Answer no if any allow or approval decision depends on a server hint or tool description text, including a default that auto-approves tools marked read-only.
checks.counter_search: Searched readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, annotations; only metadata-scan.ts reads annotations, for injection scanning, never for decisions.
checks.note: Approval decisions key on tool name from policy config, not server hints

checks.check: File access is limited to named directories, not the whole filesystem.
checks.verify: 1) Find file tools and mounts (`allowed_directories`, `cwd`, `open(`, `fs.`, `os.ReadFile`, container `volumes`, `mountPath`). 2) Check paths are resolved (`realpath`, `resolve`, `filepath.Clean`) then compared to named directories. 3) Answer no if access is unrestricted, `/` or home is mounted, the check is a string `startsWith`/prefix test without resolving `..` and symlinks, or a shell tool bypasses it.
checks.counter_search: Searched for file tools, hostPath, and fs use; only fixed config/prompt reads and a memory emptyDir /tmp and token mount.
checks.note: No file tools; read-only root filesystem with two small mounts

violates: Enforce a role-based allowlist

findings.title: Destructive-action interception
findings.requirement: List the high-impact operations. These include deletes, destructive database updates, force-pushes, tearing down infrastructure, payment changes, and sending anything outside. Block them by default in the execution path. Allow one only when a reviewer or system with higher authority approves that specific action. When the action runs, authorize its operation, target, and arguments, and block it if they aren't allowed. A list of blocked words or command names is not enough. Test other tools and raw API or shell paths that could do the same thing. Treat deleting audit records, or changing how long they are kept, as high-impact too. That includes asking a more powerful tool or peer to do it. Some agents can do all three of these in one context: read untrusted input, reach sensitive data or systems, and change things or talk to the outside. For those agents, treat every consequential action as high-impact. The exception is a design that stops untrusted content from picking the tool, destination, or arguments. findings.requirement: Send MCP calls through a gateway, or a similar enforcement layer, that the agent can't get around. Authenticate each caller (prove who they are), authorize each action, and validate calls and responses. Enforce rate limits and log every decision. For HTTP and OAuth, check the token's issuer, intended audience, expiry, and scopes. Use properly authorized credentials for the services behind the gateway. Never pass an unchecked token through. For local tools that talk over standard input/output (stdio), control process launch, file access, credentials, and networking in the host or sandbox. An HTTP gateway alone doesn't cover these. Test going around the gateway straight to the server, bad credentials, broken responses, and outages of the policy engine or scanner. MCP copies some request details into headers. If routing or policy uses those headers, reject any request whose headers don't match its body, before checking policy. Store any cached tool list or response separately for each authorization context. When the gateway is itself an OAuth client, check the issuer (`iss`, RFC 9207). Also protect discovery URLs against SSRF (tricking a server into calling places it shouldn't). Required checks must fail closed: if a required check can't run, block the action.

findings.title: Untrusted peer messages
findings.requirement: Authenticate the sending agent (prove its identity) on every message, even validly signed ones. Validate message types and schemas, and check what that peer is allowed to ask for. Where a replay could repeat an action, check freshness and track nonces or request IDs. Checking the sender alone doesn't stop replays. Test faked identity, replayed requests, requests across tenants, and instructions passed along by a compromised peer. Verify signed agent cards where they exist. A card says who an agent is, not what it may do. Check callback and webhook URLs against SSRF. A valid sender doesn't make a message's content trusted.

findings.requirement: Give sub-agents only the powers approved for their task. Enforce each child's role and any explicit approval from a higher authority. A parent must not gain a power it was denied just by asking a more powerful peer to act. Narrow credentials at each hop, for example with token exchange or transaction tokens. Authorize based on the original subject (the user or system whose authority is used) and the current actor. Earlier actors in a delegation chain are for the record only, not a reason to grant access. Test that escalation attempt.

findings.title: Recovery integrity
findings.requirement: If logs or checkpoints drive recovery, make them tamper-evident. Before using them, verify them against a separately protected trust anchor or signing key. Test that verification rejects changed checkpoints. It must also catch truncation, rollback to an older valid checkpoint, and replacement of a whole hash chain. For automatic recovery, confirm the destination supports idempotency: sending the same request twice has the effect of sending it once. Replay only within the destination's documented scope and time window. Confirm that actions you can't undo don't happen twice. Where support is missing or the result is unclear, check that replay pauses for reconciliation instead of sending again.

challenge.note: Searched all of agent/ (src, k8s, terraform, workflows, config) for checkpoint, replay, resume, recover, retry, idempotency, outbox, queue, pending and hash/sign. The audit recorder (src/audit/recorder.ts:62) is write-only to Firehose and S3 object lock; nothing reads it back. DynamoDB tables (approvals, budgets, control) hold authorization, quota and stop flags, not run state to resume from. Each run starts fresh: loop.ts keeps history in memory, the reminders CronJob (src/workers/reminders.ts) recomputes from the EHR each day, with backoffLimit 0 and restartPolicy Never, so a failed run is not resumed. The only retries are the Anthropic SDK maxRetries: 1 on a model call (loop.ts:15), which is not log-driven. Payments idempotency keys (executor.ts:122, eligibility-check.ts:42) are on first-attempt calls, not replay. The approval retry is model-initiated with an approval id. No log or checkpoint drives recovery and there is no automatic replay, so the N/A condition holds.
